subject.title: [Feature]: Support Anthropic native server-side tools (web_search, web_fetch, code_execution)

question: Should OpenClaw support Anthropic native server tools as a provider-owned opt-in feature, and what security/replay defaults should govern web_fetch and code_execution/PTC allowed_callers?
rationale: The request adds provider-specific config/API behavior, changes what data leaves OpenClaw, and may allow Anthropic-hosted code to invoke OpenClaw tools, so automation should not choose the permanent boundary.

options.title: Design provider-owned opt-in server tools
options.body: Keep the issue open and require a staged Anthropic plugin/transport design with explicit defaults, server-block replay semantics, and security proof before implementation.

options.title: Land only a web_search slice
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/49949 for a narrower native web_search path while leaving web_fetch and code_execution/PTC out of scope.

options.title: Defer code_execution/PTC
options.body: Allow lower-risk web_search/web_fetch exploration but require a separate maintainer security decision before allowed_callers or provider-hosted code execution support.

recommendation.title: Design provider-owned opt-in server tools
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open and require a staged Anthropic plugin/transport design with explicit defaults, server-block replay semantics, and security proof before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest current history signal on the Anthropic transport/config boundary and authored the prior keep-open review.
